headline: CBA surges to a new high while Anthropic overtakes OpenAI as the world's most valuable AI startup — big week for your portfolio.

portfolio.summary: A strong session on the ASX today, led by CBA charging to $165 — a solid 2.2% gain. Your energy ETF FUEL slipped as oil prices fell on a US-Iran ceasefire deal. Overnight on Wall Street, MSFT and TTWO both had strong nights, while GOOGL gave back nearly 2%. The broad diversified funds (VDHG, VGE, VTS) were quiet but positive.

movers.name: Commonwealth Bank of Australia
movers.note: CBA had a great session today, closing at $165.02 — up $3.61. No major company-specific news, but the broader ASX financials sector was lifted by softer expectations around how far the RBA will hike rates, which generally helps banks.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: TTWO jumped 3.7% last night to $225.95. GTA 6 hype is running hot — Rockstar's boss was out publicly teasing a PC port and online mode, and there was also a rare interview explaining the 13-year gap since GTA 5. Positive buzz for Take-Two's biggest asset.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft had a strong night, up 3.6% to $442.39. The company announced a new AI coding model at its Build developer conference, which got a warm reception from the market. AI momentum continues to drive MSFT higher.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google slipped nearly 2% last night to $382.40. Rival Anthropic made headlines by overtaking OpenAI as the world's most valuable AI startup, and Anthropic's new Claude Opus 4.8 model is being reported as beating Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro on coding benchmarks. More competitive pressure on Google's AI efforts.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL dropped 1.6% today to $8.46. Oil prices fell about 1.9% last night after reports of a US-Iran ceasefire deal eased fears of Middle East supply disruptions — less geopolitical risk means lower oil prices, which hits energy stocks.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG nudged up 0.8% to $76.00 today. Steady gains across global markets flowing through to this diversified fund.

markets.summary: Last night on Wall Street, both the S&P 500 and NASDAQ edged up slightly — nothing dramatic but still holding near highs. Gold is surging, up nearly 2% to a remarkable US$4,588/oz. Oil fell on ceasefire news. The Aussie dollar is stronger at 71.86 US cents, which is worth keeping an eye on for your US holdings. ASX 200 data wasn't available for today's close.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session — a modest gain, market holding firm near record levels.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Last night's session — tech stocks barely moved overall, though individual names like MSFT and TTWO ran hard.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil fell after reports of a US-Iran ceasefire deal reduced fears of supply disruption from the Middle East.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold is on a tear — up nearly 2% and sitting at an extraordinary level above US$4,500. Investors are parking money in safe havens.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie dollar strengthened as traders now reckon the RBA won't hike rates as aggressively as feared. A stronger AUD slightly reduces the value of your US holdings when converted back to Australian dollars.

politics.summary: The big domestic story today is a split between the major banks on RBA rate expectations — NAB is bucking consensus and flagging more hikes are possible, while the Aussie dollar is reflecting market bets that the RBA is actually close to done. Mixed signals for borrowers and investors alike.

stories.title: NAB defies consensus, flags more RBA rate hikes still possible
stories.why_it_matters: NAB is pushing back against the market narrative that the RBA is done raising rates, saying it's 'not ready to rule out' further hikes. This matters because if NAB is right, mortgage repayments could rise further for variable-rate borrowers. It also puts pressure on rate-sensitive sectors like property and banking — ironic, given CBA jumped today. Watch for RBA meeting minutes for clues.

stories.title: Australian dollar slips as RBA rate hike odds decrease
stories.why_it_matters: The Aussie dollar was under pressure earlier in the day as bond market traders reduced their bets on further RBA rate hikes. When markets think rates will stay lower, the AUD tends to weaken because Australian interest-bearing assets look less attractive to foreign investors. However, the AUD still closed stronger on the day at 71.86 US cents — suggesting other factors (like risk appetite and commodity prices) were also at play.

ai.summary: Huge week in AI — Anthropic has overtaken OpenAI as the world's most valuable AI startup, and its new Claude Opus 4.8 model is beating rivals on coding benchmarks. The AI coding race is intensifying with Microsoft, Anthropic, Google, and even Elon Musk's Grok all competing hard. Meanwhile, a fascinating experiment showed Claude was the 'safest' AI in a simulated society — Grok essentially caused its own civilisation's collapse.

stories.title: Anthropic overtakes OpenAI as world's most valuable AI startup
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic — the company behind the Claude AI assistant — has now surpassed OpenAI (maker of ChatGPT) in startup valuation. This is a big deal because for years OpenAI was seen as the unchallenged leader. Anthropic is backed by billions from Amazon and Google. For your GOOGL holding, this is a double-edged sword: Google has a financial stake in Anthropic's success, but Claude is also directly competing with Google's own Gemini AI products.

stories.title: Anthropic launches Claude Opus 4.8 — beats GPT-5.5 and Gemini 3.1 Pro on coding
stories.why_it_matters: Anthropic's new Claude Opus 4.8 model has reportedly topped benchmarks against both OpenAI's GPT-5.5 and Google's Gemini 3.1 Pro, particularly on coding tasks. This is the kind of news that matters for your GOOGL holding — Google's AI products are being outcompeted in one of the most commercially important areas (coding tools for developers). It also adds context to why GOOGL fell nearly 2% last night.

stories.title: Microsoft unveils new AI coding model at Build Conference
stories.why_it_matters: Microsoft used its annual Build developer conference to launch a new AI model specifically targeting coding — a market that's worth billions as businesses pay up for tools that write and review software. This directly contributed to MSFT's strong 3.6% night last night. For your MSFT holding, this is a clear tailwind: the market rewarded the announcement and Microsoft is staying competitive in the AI arms race.

stories.title: Researchers ran a simulated society with AI models — Claude thrived, Grok went extinct
stories.why_it_matters: Researchers put Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, and Grok in a simulated city to see how each AI-run society would evolve. Claude's society was the most stable and cooperative. Grok — Elon Musk's AI — caused societal collapse within days, with its civilisation going extinct. ChatGPT and Gemini fell somewhere in between. It's a quirky but telling experiment about the behavioural differences between AI systems — relevant as businesses choose which AI to trust with real decisions.

sport.summary: NRL Round 13 kicks off tonight with Sharks v Sea Eagles at 8pm. There's a big injury cloud over the Sharks and NSW Blues after Nicho Hynes' replacement shone but hooker Cam Brailey suffered a suspected broken arm. In AFL, Geelong copped a reality check in a thriller, and the AFL handed down a verdict on a controversial no-goal call.

stories.title: Sharks hooker Cam Brailey suffers suspected broken arm in win over Manly
stories.why_it_matters: Cronulla hooker Cam Brailey is feared to have broken his arm in tonight's match against Manly — a potentially season-ending injury. This is a double blow: it's a massive loss for the Sharks heading into the back half of the season, and Brailey is also a NSW State of Origin squad member, putting his rep season in serious doubt. The Sharks still won the game, with their backup playmaker stepping up in Nicho Hynes' absence.

stories.title: NRL Round 13 tips: Ricky Stuart's blow-up expected to get a reaction
stories.why_it_matters: Round 13 tippers are pointing to Raiders v Cowboys as the most intriguing match, with Raiders coach Ricky Stuart reportedly having a 'big blow-up' during the week that pundits expect to fire up his team. Raiders host the Cowboys on Sunday at GIO Stadium. Also worth watching: Panthers v Warriors at Commbank Stadium on Sunday evening — Panthers are heavy favourites.

stories.title: AFL: Geelong cops reality check in epic thriller
stories.why_it_matters: Geelong were taken to the limit in what's being described as an AFL 'epic' this week, suffering a loss that brings them back to earth after a strong start to the season. No specific scoreline available from the article, but the result is significant in the context of the premiership race — the Cats are no longer unbeatable.

stories.title: AFL hands down verdict on controversial no-goal call — rules it an 'extraordinary error'
stories.why_it_matters: The AFL today handed down its review of a controversial no-goal decision from a recent match, calling it an 'extraordinary error' by officiating. The AFL's verdict is notable because it's a rare public admission of a significant officiating mistake. No detail on which clubs were affected is available from the headline alone, but it adds to the ongoing conversation about the standard of AFL officiating in 2026.

watch_today.title: MSFT: AI coding momentum is real — hold confidently
watch_today.detail: Microsoft's Build conference announcement of a new AI coding model got a strong market reaction last night (+3.6%). This isn't a one-off — it's part of a sustained AI strategy that's working. No reason to sell. If you've been sitting on the fence about adding more, the fundamentals remain strong.

watch_today.title: GOOGL: Under genuine competitive pressure from Anthropic
watch_today.detail: Google fell nearly 2% last night as Anthropic officially overtook OpenAI in valuation and its new Claude Opus 4.8 beat Gemini 3.1 Pro on coding benchmarks. Google's AI moat is being challenged. That said, Google has a stake in Anthropic AND its own AI products, so it's not all bad. Hold for now — no need to panic — but this is worth monitoring closely over coming weeks.

watch_today.title: TTWO: GTA 6 hype building — PC and online mode teased
watch_today.detail: Take-Two's stock is up 3.7% last night and the GTA 6 PC port and online mode tease from Rockstar's boss is adding fuel to the fire. GTA 6 is shaping up to be one of the biggest game launches ever. Hold — the story is still playing out and the positive catalyst is intact.

watch_today.title: FUEL.AX: Oil fell on US-Iran ceasefire news — watch the situation
watch_today.detail: Crude oil dropped 1.9% after reports of a US-Iran ceasefire deal reduced Middle East supply risk. FUEL.AX fell 1.6% today as a result. If the ceasefire holds, oil prices could stay under pressure. If it breaks down (these things often do), oil snaps back. Keep an eye on Middle East news this week before making any moves.

watch_today.title: AUD strengthening — slightly reduces the value of your US holdings
watch_today.detail: The Aussie dollar is now at 71.86 US cents, up 0.75% today. A stronger AUD means your US-denominated holdings (GOOGL, MSFT, TTWO) are worth slightly less when converted back to Australian dollars. Nothing to act on right now, but worth being aware of if the AUD keeps climbing.
